content: Bread dough rises because yeast, a living microorganism, consumes sugars within the mixture and releases carbon dioxide gas as a byproduct. This gas gets trapped in the gluten network, causing the dough to expand and become airy. Bakers let the dough rest to allow this fermentation process to fully develop, which strengthens the structure and improves flavor. This resting period ensures the final loaf has a light, fluffy texture rather than being dense and heavy.
